newsitem.title: USA: Oil tanker still leaking fuel at Portland, Maine. [CORRECTED 07:56 GMT 28/9]
newsitem.headline: Oil tanker still leaking fuel at Portland, Maine. [CORRECTED 07:56 GMT 28/9]

text.p: An oil tanker that collided with a drawbridge in Portland, Maine, earlier Friday, continued to leak heating oil into Portland Harbor, Coast Guard officials said.

The vessel, named the Julie-N, was carrying approximately 210,000 barrels of No. 2 distillate fuel when it collided with the bridge, and not 750,000 barrels, as the Coast Guard had originally reported.
Portland Harbor remained closed as a result of the spill.
Officials said they had no estimate of the volume of oil spilled, but he confirmed that there were gashes in two of the ship's fuel tanks.
"The preliminary damage survey of the vessel indicates that there was damage to no more than two tanks of the vessel," said Coast Guard Chief Warrant Officer Charles Rathgeber.
"There is no danger of loss of the vessel or of release of all of the cargo," he added. Two containment booms had been deployed around the spill site.
Rathgeber said "significant" oil spills such as this one are rare in Portland Harbor.
"This is a very uncommon spill for this area," he said.

The accident occurred at approximately 1115 EDT/1515 GMT, officials said. Earlier Friday, officials reported that the vessel was leaking some 1,000 barrels of oil per hour into the harbor, but they later said they were unable to establish the rate of leakage.

It was unclear what type of fuel was leaking into the water, but officials said it was likely one of the vessel's own fuel tanks had been damaged during the collision, spilling heavier bunker fuel into the water along with the vessel's own distillate cargo.
The Julie-N is owned by Amity Products Carriers, Inc, a subsidiary of Overseas Shipholders Group Inc and managed by Maritime Overseas Corp, a privately held company. (Corrects name of ship owner)
The ship's cargo had been loaded in Amuay Bay, Venezuela, the ship's most recent port of call before it arrived in Portland Harbor, the official said.
The vessel was chartered by Global Petroleum Corp, he added. Officials at Global could not be reached for comment. It had been scheduled to discharge the cargo at Sprague Oil in Portland.
Meanwhile, environmental officials in Maine said they had closed the harbor to lobster fishing due to the oil spill.
Clam fishing had already been suspended due to recent heavy rains in the area.
